analysis: The trial succeeded with host macro validation HR@10=0.5675, improving on the supplied previous result of 0.5613 by 0.0062, but remaining 0.0125 below the stated best of 0.5800. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV=0.6500, Industrial_and_Scientific=0.6200, Electronics=0.4200, and CDs_and_Vinyl=0.5800. Electronics remained weakest and declined from the supplied previous 0.4300. The result supports a modest aggregate benefit from recent-item fusion in this run, but does not establish recent-identity dilution as the cause of earlier performance. Allocated GPU time was 344.04 seconds.
code_summary: One independently trained masked Transformer per category uses bidirectional relative-position attention, tied item embeddings, and jointly learned item biases. A new jointly trained path finds each position's nearest preceding visible item in the corrupted sequence, excluding padding and masks. Its embedding passes through a tanh projection and is blended with the backbone output by a learned sigmoid gate; positions without a predecessor retain the backbone output. Final and auxiliary masked queries share this fusion. Training settings and sampled-softmax objective were retained. Checks cover predecessor indices, hidden-label independence, finite gradients, backbone attention equivalence, and checkpoint reload. Exported prediction reconstructs the architecture and strictly loads one selected checkpoint per category, with no ensemble or separately fitted scorer.
